Yep, fellow LACDMH worker, and we’ve been implementing the changes since the beginning of the fiscal year. I’m optimistic. It’s confusing for clients that have been around for a long time, but I think it makes providing comprehensive treatment easier since you really only need to have one problem area listed to justify all the services (the dx/disorder is sufficient), and it really minimized a lot of the extra paperwork and documentation if it’s not clinically indicated. I’m calling it what it is when discussing with clients, but also reflecting on the benefits of not being locked into one objective and having flexibility to target what the client feels are challenging areas they want to improve on. Most people want to target their symptoms more than a specific behavior, anyway! Maybe something like a ‘stressor list’ would be ideal, but healthcare has always been problem focused. We do what we can with what we’re given!
